newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Rockets hit Israel, Netanyahu threatens response.
newsitem.headline: Rockets hit Israel, Netanyahu threatens response.

text.p: Pro-Iranian Hizbollah fighters in Lebanon rained scores of Katyusha rockets on northern Israel on Tuesday, wounding at least one civilian and prompting an Israeli threat to respond.

The twin morning barrages, about an hour apart, followed a day of violence in Lebanon that killed at least 10 civilians, seven of them in shelling by pro-Israeli militia of the southern port city of Sidon.

Israel, preoccupied by its security crisis with Palestinian President Yasser Arafat, distanced itself from Monday's fighting but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu sounded a warning that he would not tolerate attacks on Israeli civilians.

"The prime minister said Israel will respond severely to attacks on civilian lives, and Israel hopes this message will be absorbed on the other side in all of its meaning," Netanyahu's spokesman said in a statement.
The statement said the Israeli leader saw his immediate task as stopping a "circle of deterioration" which "doesn't serve the interests of either side".
The Katyushas hit the main border town of Kiryat Shmona and the western Galilee, sending residents scurrying for shelters.
A man who was driving to work when the Katyushas fell was slightly hurt. A house in Kiryat Shmona took a direct hit, witnesses said.
The second attack caused no casualties or damage, residents said, while in Lebanon pro-Israeli militia sources said a 65-year-old woman was also wounded.
"At seven o'clock we heard on the news on the television that it's quiet, everything's OK," a resident of Kiryat Shmona told Israeli army radio.
"And then precisely three or four minutes later there was a barrage of Katyushas, at least 20 or 30, a quantity I've never heard before," the man said.

Hizbollah is fighting to oust Israeli troops and their South Lebanon Army (SLA) militia allies from a 15-km (nine-mile) deep Israeli occupation zone set up inside Lebanon with the declared aim of preventing guerrilla attacks on northern Israel.

"The Islamic Resistance declares openly that it shelled the settlements in north occupied Palestine with a number of Katyusha rockets, causing many casualties," a Hizbollah (Party of God) spokesman said in Beirut.
A spokesman for the U.N. Interim Forces in Lebanon (UNIFIL) said about 80 Katyusha rockets were fired from several locations in south Lebanon and some had landed in northern Israel.

Seven Lebanese civilians, including a two-month-old boy, were killed when forces under the command of SLA leader Antoine Lahd shelled Sidon on Monday from the area of Jezzine, just north of Israel's occupation zone.
Israel strongly denied firing those shells and blamed the incident on Lahd militiamen beyond its control.

Israeli military officials said Lahd's men were apparently avenging the deaths of three youths killed by a roadside bomb in the Jezzine area earlier on Monday. The army accused Hizbollah of carrying out that attack.
The spiral of violence contravenes an agreement not to target civilians which the parties to the conflict reached after Israel launched a bloody offensive in Lebanon in April 1996.
The tension deflected attention from Israel's stand-off with Arafat's Palestinian Authority after a double suicide bombing in Jerusalem last month.
Israel was scheduled on Tuesday to transfer $12 million, or about 30 percent, of funds owed to the Authority which it froze after the bombing as part of an economic and security clampdown.
Netanyahu ordered the payment in response to what Israel says is "partial cooperation" by the Palestinians on security.
Israel has called on Arafat to launch a tough crackdown on suspected Moslem militants from the Hamas and Islamic Jihad groups, something the Palestinian president has refused to do.

Palestinian officials welcomed the financial transfer but said Israel should lift its sanctions in their entirety, including a closure of the West Bank and Gaza that has prevented tens of thousands of Palestinians from reaching jobs in Israel.
"Israel has undertaken a process of putting the entire Palestinian people in one jail," a Palestinian Authority official, Hisham Abdel Razik, told Israel Radio.
"I think that what the prime minister wants is for the Palestinian people to fight one another and not more than that," he said.
